summary: All claims verify across all 3 sources. The allowlist warning is a checker limitation, not a content problem -- see editor_notes.

findings.message: Sources not in allowlist (checker limitation, judged acceptable)
findings.details: medium.com: this URL is Expedia's own official engineering blog, published under the verified medium.com/expedia-group-tech publication. The allowlist file already has a precedent entry for medium.com/airbnb-engineering (and I added a matching medium.com/expedia-group-tech entry), but scripts/chief_editor_review.ts and scripts/validate_submissions.ts both match allowlist entries against url.hostname only, never the path -- so path-scoped Medium entries have never actually matched and this warning will keep firing regardless. This is a pre-existing gap in the checker (not something I'm authorized to fix without being asked), not a signal that the source is untrustworthy: it is Expedia's own verified corporate engineering publication, a legitimate primary source for the company's own product announcement.

content_preview.title: Expedia Open-Sources an LLM-Powered GraphQL Mocking Tool as Airbnb and a Draft Spec Chart Different Designs
content_preview.summary: Expedia's mockql-rs uses an LLM to fill in GraphQL schema fields marked with @mock, joining Airbnb's build-time directive and an early-stage GraphQL Foundation RFC.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Expedia Group has open-sourced [mockql-rs](https://github.com/ExpediaGroup/mockql-rs), a command-line tool that uses a large language model to fill in mock data for GraphQL fields marked with a custom `@mock` directive, according to a [blog post](https://medium.com/expedia-group-tech/focus-on-the-feature-not-the-fixture-genai-powered-graphql-mocks-ea069670af02) by Expedia engineer Samuel Vazquez. The release adds a third distinct approach to LLM-generated GraphQL mocking alongside A...

editor_notes.content_quality: Thorough, well-organized News piece comparing three independently-converging technical approaches to the same problem, with clear attribution of each design decision to its source.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 snapshots directly. Expedia's blog post confirms the origin-story quote, the four-step process description, the 'can't hallucinate fields' quote, and the 'LLMs are bad at inventing shapes' quote verbatim. The GitHub repo confirms the Apache-2.0 license in visible text and the May 2026 creation date via structured metadata (2026-05-08T in the raw HTML, not visible as rendered README text). InfoQ confirms the Airbnb @generateMock/Niobe details, the RFC's Stage-0/strawman/no-champion status, and the __graphql_mocks__ directory mechanism verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics trace verbatim to their cited sources. No hallucinations or misattributions found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; the Analysis section identifies the common structural driver (GraphQL's typed schema) without favoring any of the three competing designs.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate -- no prior archive coverage of GraphQL mocking tools.
recommendations: Flagging for awareness (not requesting action): scripts/chief_editor_review.ts and scripts/validate_submissions.ts match source_allowlist.txt entries against hostname only, so path-scoped entries like medium.com/airbnb-engineering and the medium.com/expedia-group-tech I added never actually suppress the 'not in allowlist' warning. This is a latent gap worth fixing in the checker itself at some point, but is out of scope for this review.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve. Every quote and specific verified verbatim across all three sources; no corrections needed.
